mainTopic: Animal blemishes involving bone, tails, warts in the eye, and uneven body parts
overview: The amud opens with a story: an animal's lower jaw stuck out past its upper jaw, and the חכמים ruled it a מום. רב פפא explains that this differs from a protruding lip, which counts only for a כהן, because the jaw has bone in it. A new משנה then rules on a doubled ear and on a goat's tail. רב פפא explains that a pig-like tail means a curled tail. רב הונא's joint counts for a tail are refuted by a ברייתא, which shows that the משנה's 'three joints' refers to a lamb. Another משנה lists more blemishes, starting with a wart in the eye. The גמרא works through several answers to resolve a contradiction about warts. It ends with a three-way rule: a wart in the black of the eye is a full מום, a wart in the white with a hair only makes the animal unfit for the מזבח, and a wart in the white without a hair is no blemish at all. The amud closes with definitions of uneven eyes and testicles, and a new משנה saying that a calf's short tail is not a מום.

steps.title: The incident of the protruding lower jaw
steps.stepSummary: A בכור animal's lower jaw stuck out past its upper jaw. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they ruled that it is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was also a case where the lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they said: this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a version of the משנה with a story. The ruling in the story is that a lower jaw sticking out past the upper jaw counts as a מום in an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a מום matters because a בכור with a מום may be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש. This ruling is the base text that the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a real case that happened

phrases.english: And there was also an incident
where the lower jaw stuck out past the upper one

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages
and they said: This is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of mouth and jaw blemishes from the preceding משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal whose lower jaw protrudes beyond its upper jaw has a מום

steps.title: A protruding lip is a blemish only for a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a protruding lip is listed as a מום for a person. That rule comes from the verse 'איש איש מזרע אהרן', which applies only to people. So why would it count for an animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned this rule about a person: if his upper lip sticks out past the lower, or the lower sticks out past the upper, it is a blemish. That rule is for a person, because the verse says 'any man of the seed of אהרן.' This means a כהן must look like the rest of אהרן's descendants. But for an animal, no such rule applies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling in step 1. A protruding lip is a known מום for a כהן, but the reason behind it seems to apply only to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The human rule is based on a special verse: a כהן must look normal, 'equal' to other descendants of אהרן. Animals have no such appearance requirement. So a protruding lip should not make an animal blemished.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any man of the seed of אהרן' (ויקרא כב:ד)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a protruding lip is a מום at all. Everyone agrees it is a מום for a person. The question is only whether that rule carries over to an animal.

phrases.english: But it is regarding a person that we learned:
his upper lip sticks out past the lower,
or the lower sticks out past the upper —
this is a blemish.
It is regarding a person that it is written:
"Any man of the seed of Aaron"
a man who is equal to (looks like) the seed of Aaron
but with an animal, not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a protruding lower jaw is a מום in an animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source for a protruding lip being a מום is a verse that applies only to people, so it should not apply to animals

steps.title: Bone versus no bone
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers: the animal case involves a jaw bone that sticks out, which is a real מום even for an animal. The human case is a fleshy lip with no bone, which is a מום only for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is not difficult. This case is where there is bone in it; that case is where there is no bone in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the challenge by showing the two rulings are about different cases. The animal ruling is about protruding bone, and the human ruling is about protruding flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the protruding part contains bone, it is a real physical defect, so it is a מום even for an animal. When only the flesh of the lip sticks out, the only problem is appearance, and that counts only for a כהן because of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not conflict
This one... that one; used to split two sources into different cases

steps.whatToRemember: A protruding jaw that has bone is a מום even for an animal. A protruding lip with no bone is a מום only for a כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same idea, bone versus no bone, comes up right away in the next משנה about a doubled ear.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult;
this is where there is bone in it,
that is where there is no bone in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two rulings deal with different physical situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seem to be about the same defect, so the animal ruling seems to borrow a rule meant only for people
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal ruling is about protruding bone, a real defect. The human ruling is about a protruding fleshy lip, an appearance issue that applies only to a כהן

steps.title: A doubled ear on a young goat
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a young goat's ear is doubled, it is a מום only if the extra part has its own bone (cartilage).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a young goat's ear was doubled, the חכמים said: when it is one bone, it is a blemish; when it has no bone, it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a young goat whose ear looks doubled, like two ears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in רב פפא's answer, bone is the deciding factor. An extra ear part with its own bone or cartilage is a real defect. A flap of skin alone is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'; marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the ear of the young goat was doubled,
the Sages said:
when it is one bone, it is a blemish;

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֶצֶם — אֵינוֹ מוּם.
phrases.english: when it has no bone, it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה; it echoes the bone and no-bone distinction from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubled ear is a מום only if the extra part has its own bone

steps.title: A pig-like or very short tail
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל rules that a young goat's tail is a מום if it looks like a pig's tail, or if it does not have three joints.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל says: the tail of a young goat that looks like a pig's tail, or that does not have three joints, is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the view of רבי חנניא בן גמליאל about blemishes of the tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate tail defects are listed. The first is a tail shaped like a pig's tail; the גמרא in step 7 explains what that means. The second is a tail so short that it has fewer than three vertebrae (חוליות).

keyTerms.meaning: Vertebrae; the joints of the spine or tail

steps.whatToRemember: A goat's tail that looks like a pig's tail, or that has fewer than three joints, is a מום according to רבי חנניא בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר,
phrases.english: the tail of a young goat that looks like that of a pig,
or that does not have three joints —
this is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with another blemish, this time of the tail
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat's tail that looks like a pig's tail, or that has fewer than three joints, is a מום

steps.title: Swelling from air or bone, and doubled ears
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that swelling from air is not a מום, but swelling from bone is. It also gives a cartilage rule for doubled ears.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: If the animal's mouth or legs are swollen, it depends on the cause. If the swelling is from air, it is not a מום. If it is from bone, it is a מום. If its ears are doubled, one cartilage makes it a מום, and two cartilages do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that adds two more rules about blemishes on a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the cause of the swelling. Swelling from air is temporary and goes away, so it is not a מום. Swelling from bone is a permanent change to the body, so it is a מום. This matches the earlier idea from רב פפא that bone makes a defect count as a real מום for an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of wind or air (a temporary puffiness)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
If its mouth is swollen and its legs are swollen,
if it is due to wind (air), it is not a blemish;
if it is due to bone, this is a blemish.
If its ears are doubled,
with one cartilage, this is a blemish;
with two cartilages, it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה with a ברייתא that adds more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swelling from air is not a מום, but swelling from bone is. A doubled ear with one cartilage is a מום, and with two cartilages it is not.

steps.title: What counts as a pig-like tail
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a tail is 'like a pig's' because it curls, not because it is thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says that a kid's tail that looks like a pig's tail is a מום. רב פפא said: Don't think this means a thin tail. It means a curled tail, even if the tail is thick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's words from the משנה. Then רב פפא explains which feature of a pig's tail the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways a tail could 'look like a pig's': it could be thin, or it could be curled. רב פפא says the key feature is the curl. So a thick goat tail that curls up still counts as a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: The tail of a young goat (kid)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'like a pig' means thin. According to רב פפא, the shape (the curl) is what matters, not how thick the tail is.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר.
phrases.english: The tail of a kid that resembles that of a pig.
Rav Pappa said:
Do not say that it means where the tail is thin;
rather, it means where the tail is curled,
even though it is thick.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה's tail case and defines its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A kid's tail is 'like a pig's' when it is curled, even if it is thick.

steps.title: רב הונא's joint count for a kid and a lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a kid's tail with two joints is a מום, and a lamb's tail with three joints is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Or if the tail does not have three joints.' רב הונא said: For a kid, two joints is a מום and three is not. For a lamb, three joints is a מום and four is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, and רב הונא gives exact joint counts for a גדי and a טלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the משנה's 'three joints' as referring to a גדי, so for a גדי, fewer than three joints is a מום. He then sets a stricter number for a טלה, which has a longer tail and needs four joints. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Joints or vertebrae of the tail
Etc. (the quote from the משנה continues)

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁלֹשׁ חוּלְיוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Or if it does not have three joints, etc.
Rav Huna said:
In a kid, two joints is a blemish;
three joints is not a blemish.
In a lamb, three joints is a blemish;
four joints is not a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁלֹשׁ חוּלְיוֹת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second half of the משנה's tail rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kid: 2 joints is a מום and 3 is not. Lamb: 3 joints is a מום and 4 is not.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives lower joint counts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a kid needs only two joints and a lamb needs only three, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: For a kid, one joint is a מום and two is not. For a lamb, two joints is a מום and three is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא whose numbers are each one lower than his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, a kid with two joints has a מום. According to the ברייתא, that same kid is fine. The same gap exists for the lamb. So the ברייתא directly contradicts רב הונא's numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
In a kid, one joint is a blemish;
two joints is not a blemish.
In a lamb, two joints is a blemish;
three joints is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's numbers from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's joint counts for a גדי and a טלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sets each threshold one joint lower, so the cases where רב הונא says there is a מום, the ברייתא says there is none.

steps.title: רב הונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a final refutation of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב הונא's view cannot stand against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered on his behalf. The ברייתא's numbers become the accepted rule: a kid needs two joints and a lamb needs three.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 9 against רב הונא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is the rule: a kid with one joint has a מום, and a lamb with two joints has a מום.

steps.title: How the משנה misled רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא assumed the whole משנה was about a kid. In fact, the 'three joints' clause is about a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה misled רב הונא. He thought that since the first part is about a kid, the last part must also be about a kid. But that is not so. The first part is about a kid, and the last part is about a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a great אמורא like רב הונא made this mistake. It also shows the correct way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first clause (the pig-like tail) is about a גדי. רב הונא assumed the next clause ('three joints') kept the same subject. But it actually switches to a טלה, which fits the ברייתא exactly: a lamb with fewer than three joints has a מום.
steps.whatToRemember: Tail joints: a גדי needs two joints (one is a מום), and a טלה needs three joints (two is a מום). The משנה's 'three joints' refers to the טלה, not the גדי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume each clause of a משנה keeps the same subject. Here the subject changes from גדי to טלה without saying so.

phrases.english: And as for Rav Huna, the mishna misled him;
he thought:
since the first clause is about a kid,
the latter clause is also about a kid;
but it is not so:
the first clause is about a kid, and the latter clause is about a lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation, explains the source of רב הונא's error and gives the correct reading of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's first clause is about a גדי and its second clause is about a טלה, which matches the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס lists more blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס lists several blemishes: a wart in the eye, a damaged leg bone, a dislocated jaw, and uneven eyes or ears that you can see by looking.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says that these count as blemishes. An animal with a wart in its eyes. One whose foreleg or hind leg bone was damaged. One whose jawbone was dislocated. One with one eye large and one small, or one ear large and one small. This applies only when the difference is visible by sight, not when it can only be found by measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס adds more physical defects that make an animal a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most items here are clear physical damage. The uneven eye or ear case has a limit. It counts only if a person can see the difference just by looking. If the difference is so small that only a measurement shows it, it is not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: By sight, visible to the eye

steps.whyThisMatters: The case of a wart in the eye becomes the subject of the whole גמרא that follows.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
one that has a wart in its eyes,
and one whose foreleg or hind leg bone was damaged,
and one whose jawbone was dislocated,
one of its eyes large and one small,
one of its ears large and one small,
visible by sight, but not only by measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה continues the list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wart in the eye, a damaged limb bone, a dislocated jaw, and visibly uneven eyes or ears are blemishes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה on uneven testicles, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if one testicle is twice the size of the other, it is a מום. The חכמים do not accept this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if, of its two testicles, one is as large as two of the other, it is a blemish. But the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds one more blemish to the list. The משנה then tells us that the חכמים rejected his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a disagreement. For רבי יהודה, a large difference in size counts as a defect. The חכמים do not count it, so the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
its two testicles, if one is as large
as two of the other,
but the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed case to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה counts a testicle twice the size of the other as a מום. The חכמים disagree.

steps.title: A contradiction: another משנה says a wart is not a real blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a wart can be a מום when another משנה lists warts among the defects that do not allow slaughtering a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this mean that a wart counts as a blemish? But a contradiction can be raised from another משנה: 'And these are the ones for which we do not slaughter, neither in the מקדש nor in the rest of the country: an animal with boils, and an animal with a wart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה. It points to a different משנה that seems to say the opposite about warts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats a wart in the eye as a real מום. The משנה on 41a lists a wart among defects that are not full blemishes, so a בכור with one may not be slaughtered for it. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: In the country, outside the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: 'We do not slaughter for them, neither in the מקדש nor in the country' means two things. The animal cannot be offered in the מקדש, because the defect makes it unfit for the מזבח. It also cannot be slaughtered outside as a blemished בכור, because the defect is not a full מום.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Is this to say that a wart is a blemish?
And they raised a contradiction:
And these are the ones for which we do not slaughter,
neither in the Temple nor in the country:
one with boils and one with a wart!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wart clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in our משנה that a wart in the eye is a מום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה on 41a says a wart is not a full blemish, which contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: But the Torah itself calls a wart a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. We cannot simply say a wart is not a blemish, because the Torah lists יבלת as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can you think that? Wart is written in the Torah as a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 41a משנה cannot be the full answer. This sets up the need for a distinction between two kinds of warts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we followed the 41a משנה alone, we would say a wart is never a blemish. That cannot be right, because ויקרא 22:22 lists יבלת among the blemishes. So some warts must be real blemishes, and the גמרא now has to explain which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you think so? A sign that the גמרא is rejecting an assumption

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?
Wart is written in the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that a wart is simply not a blemish.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the 41a משנה means warts are never blemishes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah explicitly lists יבלת as a blemish.

steps.title: First answer: a wart on the body or a wart in the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by location. A wart on the body is not a full blemish. A wart in the eye is a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult. That משנה is about a wart on its body. This one is about a wart in its eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer. The two sources speak about warts in different places on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 41a משנה, which says a wart is not a full blemish, is about a wart on the body. Our משנה and the Torah are about a wart in the eye, which is a real blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources speak of different cases

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
that one is on its body,
this one is in its eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּגוּפוֹ, הָא בְּעֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart on the body is not a full blemish. A wart in the eye is a blemish.

steps.title: The verse does not mention a location
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the first answer. The פסוק says 'wart' without saying where, so the body and the eye should be treated the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, the verse is written without detail. What difference does it make to me whether it is on its body or in its eye?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah writes יבלת with no mention of a body part. So there is no source for treating a wart in the eye differently from a wart on the body. The split by location has no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: Now, the verse is unspecified,
what difference is it to me if on its body
and what difference is it to me if in its eye?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי קְרָא סְתָמָא, מָה לִי בְּגוּפוֹ וּמָה לִי בְּעֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between a wart on the body and a wart in the eye.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is general, so a difference in location cannot be drawn from it.

steps.title: Second answer: a wart with a bone or a wart without one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. A wart that has a bone in it is a blemish. A wart without a bone is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult. This one is a wart that has a bone in it, and that one is a wart that does not have a bone in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the location answer with a new distinction. This time it is based on what the wart is made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the difference lies in the wart itself, not in where it sits. A hard wart with bone in it is the blemish the Torah and our משנה mean. A soft wart without bone is the minor defect in the 41a משנה. This avoids the problem of the unspecified פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: That has a bone in it
That has no bone in it

steps.whatToRemember: This bone/no-bone answer is spelled out in step 19 and then challenged in step 20. The final resolution comes in steps 21–23.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this is one that has a bone in it,
that is one that has no bone in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִית בַּהּ עֶצֶם, הָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 16 after the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the nature of the wart
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The distinction was based on location (body or eye).
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart with a bone is a blemish. A wart without a bone is not a full blemish.

steps.title: Spelling out the bone answer: eye versus body
steps.stepSummary: The verse (and our משנה) speak of a wart with a bone, and the other משנה speaks of a wart without a bone. A bony wart in the eye is a full מום. A boneless wart on the body is not a full מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wart in the verse is one that has a bone. The wart in the other משנה is one with no bone. In the eye it is a blemish. On the body it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the bone answer from the last step fits both sources: which one is talking about which kind of wart, and where it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse and our משנה, which call a wart a full מום, are talking about a wart with a bone in it. The other משנה, which says a wart does not allow slaughtering a בכור, is talking about a wart without a bone. The גמרא adds a location: in the eye it is a מום, on the body it is not a full מום, although the animal is still unfit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: That of the verse (the wart the פסוק talks about)
That has in it / that does not have in it

steps.confusionAlert: Not a full מום does not mean the animal is fine. The other משנה still makes it unfit for the מזבח. It just cannot be slaughtered and eaten as a blemished בכור.

phrases.english: The wart of the verse is one that has a bone in it,
the wart of the (other) Mishnah is one that has no bone in it;
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה that lists a wart among defects that do not allow slaughtering a בכור.

phrases.english: in its eye, it is a blemish,
on the body, it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in detail the bone/no-bone answer given in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by bone and by location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse and the other משנה seem to argue about the same kind of wart.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse means a bony wart in the eye, which is a full מום. The other משנה means a boneless wart on the body, which is not a full מום.

steps.title: A boneless wart on the body is just hanging flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a boneless wart on the body would disqualify the animal at all. It is only hanging flesh, and רבי אליעזר says hanging flesh disqualifies a person (a כהן) but not an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a boneless wart on the body really disqualifying? It is just hanging flesh! As we learned: רבי אליעזר says, those with hanging growths are disqualified in a person but fit in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 19, using a משנה that says hanging flesh does not disqualify an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 19, the other משנה is about a boneless wart on the body, and that משנה still treats the animal as unfit for the מזבח. But a boneless wart is just loose, dangling flesh. רבי אליעזר rules that dangling flesh makes an animal fully fit. So the other משנה could not be talking about such a wart.

keyTerms.meaning: Hanging or dangling piece of flesh or skin
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And if it has no bone and is on the body, is it disqualified?
Why, it is merely hanging flesh,
as we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
those with hanging growths are disqualified in a person,
phrases.notes: A כהן with this cannot serve.

phrases.english: but fit in an animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the other משנה (animal unfit for the מזבח) is about a boneless wart on the body.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A boneless wart is just hanging flesh, and רבי אליעזר says hanging flesh leaves an animal fully fit. So it cannot be the case of a משנה that makes the animal unfit.

steps.title: Both cases are in the eye: black part versus white part
steps.stepSummary: New answer: both sources are about a wart in the eye. Our משנה (full מום) means a wart in the black of the eye. The other משנה (unfit for the מזבח but not a full מום) means a wart in the white of the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are in the eye, and there is no difficulty: this one is in the black part, that one is in the white part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the body explanation and gives a new answer that puts both cases in the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a wart on the body is too minor to disqualify, both sources must be about the eye. The difference is which part of the eye. A wart in the black of the eye (the pupil) is a full מום. A wart in the white of the eye is the lesser case from the other משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
The black part of the eye (the pupil)
The white part of the eye

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are in its eye,
and it is not difficult:
this one is in the black, that one is in the white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the body/eye split, which step 20 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New אוקימתא: a different split by location inside the eye
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The less serious wart is on the body.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are in the eye. A wart in the black is a full מום, and a wart in the white only makes the animal unfit for the מזבח.

steps.title: There are no blemishes in the white of the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that there is an accepted rule that the white of the eye has no blemishes at all. So a wart there should not make the animal unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are no blemishes in the white!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 21 with a known rule about the white of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said a wart in the white of the eye makes the animal unfit for the מזבח. But an established rule says nothing in the white of the eye counts as a blemish. That would mean the animal is fully fit, which contradicts the other משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no blemishes in the white of the eye

phrases.english: But there are no blemishes in the white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the white-of-the-eye case from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a wart in the white of the eye makes the animal unfit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted rule says the white of the eye has no blemishes, so a wart there should not make the animal unfit at all.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a wart with hair versus a wart without hair
steps.stepSummary: Both the rule (no blemishes in the white) and the other משנה are about the white of the eye. ריש לקיש explains that a wart with a hair makes the animal unfit, and a wart without a hair does not. Our משנה, the full מום, stays in the black of the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both are in the white. And ריש לקיש said: it is not difficult. This one has a hair, that one has no hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the white-of-the-eye case but splits it again, quoting ריש לקיש: hair or no hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that there are no blemishes in the white is about a plain wart without a hair. The other משנה, which makes the animal unfit, is about a wart in the white that has a hair growing from it. Our משנה's full מום is still a wart in the black of the eye, so all three sources fit.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (רבי שמעון בן לקיש), known for sharp answers

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: a wart in the black of the eye is a full מום, so a בכור may be slaughtered for it. A wart in the white with a hair makes the animal unfit for the מזבח but is not a full מום. A wart in the white without a hair is not a blemish at all.

phrases.english: Rather: both this and that are in the white,
and Reish Lakish said: it is not difficult,
this one is where it has a hair,
that one is where it has no hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בַּלָּבָן, וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by splitting the white-of-the-eye case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: splitting the case by hair or no hair
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wart in the white of the eye is the same, so the rule and the other משנה clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart in the white with a hair makes the animal unfit. A wart in the white without a hair is not a blemish.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Black of the eye: full מום. White with hair: unfit for the מזבח only. White without hair: no blemish.

steps.title: How big is large and how small is small for an eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about one eye being large and the other small. A ברייתא defines the sizes: large means like a calf's eye, small means like a goose's eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one of its eyes is large, and so on. It was taught: large means like a calf's eye, small means like a goose's eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The wart discussion is finished, and the גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It quotes the line and then brings a ברייתא that defines its words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that unequal eyes are a מום but does not say how big the difference must be. The ברייתא gives clear measures. An eye as big as a calf's eye counts as large, and one as small as a goose's eye counts as small.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the quote continues in the משנה)
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: "One of its eyes is large," etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which sets up the explanation that follows.

phrases.english: It was taught: large means like that of a calf,
small means like that of a goose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the wart discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large means like a calf's eye, and small means like a goose's eye.

steps.title: How big a testicle difference do רבנן allow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about one ear being large. That line leads into רבי יהודה's view on uneven testicles, which רבנן reject. The גמרא asks how big a difference רבנן allow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One of its ears is large,' and so on. And according to רבנן, how big can the difference be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks a clarifying question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of the משנה. There, רבי יהודה says that if one testicle is double the size of the other, it is a מום, and רבנן do not accept this. If double is not a מום for רבנן, the גמרא wants to know where their limit is, or whether they have any limit at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.', meaning the quote continues in the משנה
Up to how much? What is the limit?

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted words are about ears, but the question 'עד כמה' is about the testicles. רבי יהודה's dispute with רבנן on the testicles appears in the same line of the משנה, covered by the 'וכו׳'.

phrases.english: 'One of its ears is large,' etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line includes רבי יהודה's view on the testicles.

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, up to how much?
phrases.notes: How big a size difference still does not count as a מום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the eye-size line of the משנה to the next line, about ears and testicles.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The limit of size difference between the testicles that רבנן still consider fit.

steps.title: Even if the second is as small as a bean, the animal is fit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים: even if the smaller testicle is only the size of a bean, the animal is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say, even if the second one is only like a bean, the animal is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. Following רבנן's approach, the difference can be huge and the animal is still fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן there is basically no size limit. As long as the second testicle exists, even if only bean-sized, there is no מום. This shows why they rejected רבי יהודה's 'double' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
'Others', a name for a תנא (traditionally רבי מאיר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: one testicle double the other is a מום. רבנן (as explained by אחרים): even a bean-sized second testicle is fit.

phrases.english: It was taught: Others say:
Even if the second one is not
more than a bean, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a second testicle the size of a bean is fit, so for רבנן size difference is not a מום.

steps.title: New משנה: a calf's short tail is not a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a calf whose tail does not reach the leg joint is not blemished. Most calves are like this, and their tails stretch as they grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A calf's tail that does not reach the leg joint: the חכמים said, most calves are like this. As long as they keep growing, their tails stretch out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a short tail on a calf is not a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a tail that is too short might look like a defect. But since almost all young calves have short tails that lengthen with growth, this is simply normal for a calf. Something that is the normal state of the species is not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה', marking where the משנה starts

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אמרו חכמים' is giving the reason why the short tail is NOT a מום, namely that most calves are like this. It is not declaring it a מום (see רמב״ם, ביאת מקדש ז).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle in מומין: what is normal for the animal's age or type is not a defect.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The tail of a calf
that does not reach the leg joint,
the Sages said:
most calves are like this,
phrases.notes: So it is not a מום.

phrases.english: as long as they keep growing,
their tails stretch out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of uneven body parts ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A calf's tail that does not reach the ערקוב is not a מום, because calves' tails lengthen as they grow.

steps.title: Which leg joint is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which ערקוב it was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which leg joint did they mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself stops to ask a clarifying question about the word ערקוב. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's leg has more than one joint, so 'the ערקוב' is unclear. Knowing which joint is meant tells us how long a normal tail should be.

phrases.english: Which is the leg joint they spoke of?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a key word in the ruling of step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which joint the term ערקוב refers to.

steps.title: The joint in the middle of the thigh
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says the ערקוב is the joint in the middle of the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: it is the joint in the middle of the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. It defines the ערקוב as the joint in the middle of the thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the measuring point for a calf's tail. A calf's tail that falls short of this joint is still not a מום, because it will grow.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, from a family of כהנים, who often rules on מומין

steps.whatToRemember: A calf's short tail is not a מום. The ערקוב the משנה refers to is the joint in the middle of the thigh.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
It is the leg joint in the middle of the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ערקוב is the joint in the middle of the thigh.
